text:
ConocoPhillips edged up 0.28% today, a modest gain that reflects conflicting pressures on oil stocks. The collapse of fossil fuel language from the UN climate summit (COP31) on Sunday removed a near-term regulatory risk that had been weighing on the sector, while oil prices remain relatively stable—US crude at $82/barrel and global crude at $91.80/barrel. This modest recovery comes after the stock fell 2% over the past two weeks, driven by uncertainty around climate policy and broader energy sector concerns.

The stock is caught between two longer-term currents: climate policy headwinds that discourage traditional fossil fuel investment, and growing AI-driven demand for energy infrastructure that could support oil and gas companies' future prospects. Today's small gain suggests the immediate relief from the failed climate deal outweighs those deeper structural concerns, at least for now.
